info.bio:
Todd Harry Rundgren (Upper Darby, Pennsylvania, 22 de junio de 1948) es un guitarrista, cantantautor y productor de grabación.

Rundgren fue durante toda su infancia y adolescencia un apasionado de la música, inclinándose por la que en aquellos momentos se hacía en Gran Bretaña, hasta el punto de llegar a idealizar el lugar. Le apasionan especialmente los Beatles, los Kinks o The Who, así como el movimiento mod.

En 1965, con diecisiete años, forma su primera banda, Money.

scenes.name: Cantautores de los setenta
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: James Taylor se convierte, misteriosamente, en el prototipo del cantautor de los setenta; Carole King, Carly Simon y Don McLean, sobrevalorados. Las innovaciones llegan del oeste: Randy Newman y sus viñetas urbanas con fusión de estilos populares, Shawn Phillips, J.J. Cale y su estilo «laid-back», Gram Parsons, Emmylou Harris, Roger McGuinn, Jackson Browne (Late For The Sky) y, sobre todo, Tom Waits, discípulo de Beefheart y cronista de marginados (Swordfishtrombones, Rain Dogs). Excéntricos como Todd Rundgren y Annette Peacock; en Gran Bretaña, Peter Hammill, Anthony Moore, Richard Thompson, Robert Calvert, John Cale, Kevin Coyne, Elton John y los ex Beatles. El realismo de Bruce Springsteen, verdadero heredero de Woody Guthrie y del blues, y la escuela italiana de cantautores (De André, Guccini, Battisti, Sorrenti).

podcast.title: Producer for Wave
podcast.body: Todd Rundgren, known as a "pop guy" rather than a punk producer, produced Patti Smith's 1979 album *Wave*. His involvement contributed to the album's smoother, more melodic sound, departing from the raw punk aesthetic of her earlier work. "It was produced by Todd Rungren who was not punk but he was more of a pop guy."

podcast.title: Self-Funded "Bat Out of Hell" Production
podcast.body: As the producer for Meat Loaf's debut album *Bat Out of Hell*, Rock and Roll Hall of Famer Todd Rundgren discovered that Meat Loaf did not actually have a record deal with RCA as he initially believed. Convinced that the album "needs to be made," Rundgren personally agreed to pay for its recording. "The producer was rock and roll, Hall of Famer Todd Rungren, who ended up agreeing to paying for the recording of Bad Out of Hell himself. Because originally he thought that Meatloaf had a record deal with RCA, but he didn't. So Rungren's like, well, this needs to be made. So I'll pay for it."

xref.title: Precursors to Other Powerpop Bands
xref.body: Big Star predated other successful Powerpop bands of the 1970s, such as Badfinger, Todd Rundgren, The Raspberries, Cheap Trick, and The Knack, establishing the genre's foundation before its wider recognition. "There were other Powerpop bands in the 70s who had hits. There was Bad Finger and Todd Rungren. We had the raspberries, Cheap Trick, the Nack, but Big Star was there before all of them."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Production Philosophy - Collaborative Approach
xref.body: Botrell defines a record producer's responsibility as getting the "best out of the artist and musician and the songs," preferring a collaborative approach over autocratic styles like Todd Rundgren or Bob Ezrin. He encourages artists to try all ideas without argument, quickly discerning what works. "I'm a collaborative producer. So I like to work with the artist."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
